title: The 1953 DNA structure papers
summary: Three papers in Nature in 1953 belong together. Watson and Crick, "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid," proposed a double helix for DNA.
body: Three papers in Nature in 1953 belong together. Watson and Crick, "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid," proposed a double helix for DNA. Franklin and Gosling, "Molecular Configuration in Sodium Thymonucleate," reported X-ray evidence on the sodium salt of DNA. Wilkins, Stokes, and Wilson, "Molecular Structure of Deoxypentose Nucleic Acids," reported further structural evidence. The model pairs the bases so that the sequence of one strand specifies the other, which supplies a way for the molecule to be copied. How credit was divided among the people who built the model and the people who made the diffraction measurements has been argued ever since. This card states what each paper is. It does not award the argument.
